challenges.title: Our rooftop tank hits scalding by afternoon
challenges.summary: Cold showers don't exist here from May to September. The plastic tank absorbs heat all day and stays warm overnight.
challenges.source_note: Explainer, not a report: it describes the mechanism rather than a single incident. Plastic rooftop tanks absorb heat through the day and stay warm overnight because overnight minimums stay high.

media.alt: a black plastic water storage tank on a flat concrete rooftop in harsh overhead sun, heat shimmer rising off the roof

challenges.title: Metal-roofed classrooms hit 39.8C and children stop learning
challenges.summary: Measured up to 5.9C hotter than outdoors, overheated for 72.5% of occupied hours. A plywood ceiling halves that.
challenges.source_note: 16 classrooms in Accra measured over 389 days. Concrete roofs ran up to 5.8C cooler than metal; a plywood ceiling under metal halved overheating hours. The authors note the finding is meant to generalise across tropical Africa, but every number here is Ghanaian and the study makes no claim about any other country.

media.alt: a single-storey classroom with a corrugated metal roof under a white midday sun, dry red earth around it

challenges.title: The clinic's vaccine fridge runs on a generator we can only afford a few hours a day
challenges.summary: Mothers walk in and get sent home because the vaccines are out. Some never come back.
challenges.source_note: The local government generator could not reliably power the vaccine fridges. A health worker on mothers turned away during stock-outs: 'Some never showed up again.' Solar fridges are the known fix and this piece documents one being installed - the open part is the clinics that still have no power.

media.alt: a small white medical refrigerator beside a petrol generator and fuel cans in a bare rural clinic room

challenges.title: My pond's oxygen crashes at dawn and I find out when the fish float
challenges.summary: Dissolved oxygen bottoms out in the small hours. By the time anyone can see it, the loss has happened.
challenges.source_note: Fishery technician Joey de Leon: the fish 'died during the wee hours, when dissolved oxygen levels in the ponds dropped.' One operator lost 40,000 fingerlings.

media.alt: a still fish pond at first light, pale pink sky, several fish floating belly-up at the surface

challenges.title: Macaques strip the harvest and the deterrents cost more than the fruit
challenges.summary: Losses run 2,300 to 14,000 LKR a month per farm, plus 1,200 to 3,000 LKR a household on firecrackers and air rifles.
challenges.source_note: Peer-reviewed survey of commercial farms in Kurunegala District. Figures are the paper's own. The wider '93 million coconuts lost' national figure circulating in Sri Lankan press is not from this paper and is not cited here.

media.alt: macaque monkeys climbing a coconut palm and pulling at the fruit, a farm shed below

challenges.title: Ten days to clear rice stubble before wheat sowing, and burning is free
challenges.summary: Punjab needs 50,000 Happy Seeders to clear its fields in time. The government distributed 24,000.
challenges.source_note: Published 2020, so the machine counts are five years old and the shortfall may have moved. The structural trap has not: 10-15 days between rice harvest and wheat sowing, a seeder covering 10 acres a day, and a machine usable only 15 days a year so hiring centres will not buy one. Article gives Rs 1,000 rent plus Rs 2,000 diesel per acre; it does not state a purchase price.

media.alt: a flat harvested rice field of cut stubble with a tractor and seed drill at the edge, low smoky haze

challenges.title: Baboons listen for the lock beep and go for the cars that didn't chirp
challenges.summary: They already knew how to open a door. The new part is waiting to hear which ones are worth trying.
challenges.source_note: Cape Town destination manager Theuns Vivian: baboons wait for the remote-lock sound and 'If they don't hear the tweet tweet they make for the door.' Dated 2010 - the behaviour is documented here, but this source says nothing about how widespread it is now.

media.alt: a baboon sitting on the roof of a parked car at a coastal viewpoint, door slightly ajar

challenges.title: Tokyo cut its crows to under a fifth without killing them
challenges.summary: Twenty-five years of waste management and habit change did what culling did not. Worth copying where crows still win.
challenges.source_note: A December survey put Tokyo's crow population at under 20% of its early-2000s peak after a 25-year campaign. Filed at Learn rather than as an open problem: this one is largely solved in Tokyo and is here as the worked example for cities where it is not.

media.alt: tidy netted rubbish collection points on a clean city street at dawn, two crows perched on a wire above

challenges.title: The rainwater tank goes hazy and smells of sulfide by the third week
challenges.summary: Low water plus heat and the whole tank turns. Chlorinating fixes it once; nobody wants to chlorinate rainwater forever.
challenges.source_note: Forum thread, roughly 2012. Two 1,500-gallon tanks down to about a foot of water in low-90sF heat; water turned hazy and 'smells of hydrogen sulfide rather badly'. Tanks were shaded and partly buried, so sun exposure was not the cause. Old thread, but the failure mode is not dated.

media.alt: a large rainwater storage tank beside a wooden house in summer, cloudy water visible in a glass jar on a stump
